prize_parts.citation: For turning the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a chemical tool: small molecules that induce proximity between an E3 ligase and a target protein, from heterobifunctional degraders to the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: Having read the whole first round, I keep targeted protein degradation as my single part and the same three names. The chair asks for one defensible sentence that covers both strands. I think it exists: in both, a small molecule is designed or discovered to bring an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a target protein together, and the ubiquitin-transfer chemistry of the cell then does the work catalytically. Crews and Deshaies established the heterobifunctional design principle and Handa's identification of cereblon showed that the thalidomide class, already in patients, acts by the same logic. That is why the two strands read as one mechanism rather than stitched topics. The principle is general, independently reproduced in many academic and industrial laboratories, and increasingly measured in quantitative terms (ternary-complex cooperativity, ubiquitination kinetics), which is the evidence standard I apply. It has already given glue-class medicines, so clinical maturity does not depend on a heterobifunctional approval. B010 is also the only candidate that nearly every member lists as at least an acceptable alternative, which matters when a majority of five is needed, though I do not treat counts as a scientific argument.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, and I cannot confirm late-stage trial status from the material I have, so I would want the expert report to state it. The glue-class medicines were explained retrospectively, so a critic can say that the clinical record belongs to the cereblon strand and not to the design principle. Credit remains split: Sakamoto (first PROTAC), Ciulli (structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work), Gray, Ito and Kim all have real claims that a three-name limit excludes. Choosing Handa over Ciulli is a judgement about which strand needs a mechanism-defining name, not a claim that Ciulli's work is minor.

responses.point: Heiner prefers B046 (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen), accepts that the physiological claims about in-cell condensates are unsettled, and in his round-1 text asks whether PROTACs and glues should be combined and whether clinical maturity is sufficient.
responses.response: My answer to his question is that one sentence works because the chemistry is shared, and I have kept it as one part. On B046 I think the in vitro thermodynamics (valency, saturation concentration, phase diagrams) is solid and the P-granule work was a real conceptual advance. My hesitation, which round 1 did not remove, is measurement. The chair himself accepts that it is unsettled which in-cell condensates are equilibrium phase-separated and functionally essential. As someone who has seen dNTP-pool assumptions fail once measured properly, I would want that settled before a citation says the principle organizes the interior of living cells. If the committee limited the citation to the physical-chemical framework, as Emma frames it, I would find it more acceptable, but it would still be early next to B010.

responses.point: Peter prefers B035 (Buchwald, Hartwig), calls it the clearest new reaction that became routine, with clean attribution, and says he wants to see whether B010 is mature enough clinically to move it up.
responses.response: I agree with his assessment of B035: the mechanistic work on oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination is part of the achievement, the attribution is the cleanest on the list, and the Kosugi precedent can be handled by careful wording. That is why I now list B035 as an alternative; I would not oppose it as a final outcome. On maturity I would answer his B010 question directly: the cereblon-mediated medicines are in use and the mechanism is established, so the maturity test is met by that strand, and the heterobifunctional strand is supported by quantitative mechanistic work and trial activity that I want confirmed in the expert report. I also think B035 is a different kind of achievement from B010. It is a reaction for making molecules, whereas B010 gives chemists a way to act on cellular proteins, and that is why I still put B010 first.

responses.point: Johan prefers B011 with Balasubramanian and Klenerman only, citing reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis on clustered surfaces, and has narrowed to a single lineage following Heiner's argument; he lists B010 as his alternative and weighs its incomplete clinical validation.
responses.response: His narrowing to one lineage makes B011 cleaner than it was in the opening, and I think the chemistry (3'-blocked fluorescent nucleotides, surface clustering) is real chemistry rather than just a biological tool. It stays my alternative. My remaining difficulty is the one I gave in round 1: omitting Rothberg and Mayer and Ju are judgments about lineages I cannot verify from the supplied material, and the committee would face the same exclusion arguments again in the citation. I also think the fit with Chemistry rather than Medicine is a fair question that the other members have not settled. On his timing concern about B010, the quantitative mechanistic evidence and the glue medicines make me less concerned than he is, but I accept that an approved PROTAC would make the case simpler.

responses.point: Peter prefers B035 for its convergent attribution and three decades of confirmation, and says he would want an expert organometallic report on whether Buchwald and Hartwig are the decisive pair; he also notes B043 has no support beyond his own ballot.
responses.response: His point that a member should not push a configuration that the expert reports have not examined is one I take seriously, and it applies to my own work too: my statements on trial status and priority for Sakamoto, Ito and Kim come from memory. I agree that B035 is the sturdier choice if the committee weights certainty of attribution above everything else. For his B043, I said in round 1 that the science is convincing but that I did not see a basis to rank it above degraders, and nothing in the exchange has changed that, since no other member has supported it. I would not hold the Kosugi question against B035 if the expert report supports a Buchwald-Hartwig pair.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports confirm the status of heterobifunctional degrader trials and approved glue-class medicines.
Whether the committee accepts one citation sentence that covers both heterobifunctional degraders and cereblon glues; if it insists on a PROTAC-only citation, I would move Handa out for Ciulli.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; priority details for Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray are from memory and unverified.
Whether support among members for B010 as an alternative will translate into five votes, given that only two preferred it in round 1.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict to disclose. My work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is not tied to any shortlisted candidate, and I have no recorded collaboration with the credited names. No disclosure has changed since round 1.
